proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–306: spt T = spt μ_T for currents of locally finite mass), with μ_T = θH^n⌞M by Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (the sibling mass_eq_weight, Submission.rsd_massOn_eq_measure). This is the fact used in steps 2–3 of the parent proof: x ∈ spt T gives μ_T(B_r(x)) > 0, and positive density gives membership in spt T.

1. (⇒) Let x ∈ spt T. Then x ∈ U by the definition spt T = U ∖ (zero region).
Suppose, for a contradiction, that μ_T(B_r(x)) = 0 for some r > 0. Choose s ∈ (0, r) with B̄_s(x) ⊆ U (U is open) and put W := B_{s/2}(x). Then W is open, and W̄ = B̄_{s/2}(x) is compact and contained in U.
Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ∫_{M∩B_r(x)} θ dH^n = μ_T(B_r(x)) = 0.
Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. The integrand θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ of T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n vanishes on M ∖ W, and M ∩ W ⊆ M ∩ B_r(x) is H^n-null, so T(ω) = 0.
Hence W is one of the open sets whose union is the zero region, and x ∈ W. So x ∉ spt T, a contradiction. Thus μ_T(B_r(x)) > 0 for every r > 0.

2. (⇐) Let x ∈ U with μ_T(B_r(x)) > 0 for all r > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T. Then x lies in the zero region: x ∈ W₀ for an open W₀ with W̄₀ compact, W̄₀ ⊆ U, and T(ω) = 0 whenever ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and spt ω ⊆ W₀.
Choose r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ W₀. Every ω admissible for M_{B_r(x)}(T) (spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), |ω| ≤ 1) satisfies spt ω ⊆ W₀, hence T(ω) = 0. The zero form is admissible, so M_{B_r(x)}(T) = 0.
B_r(x) is open and contained in U, so the sibling mass_eq_weight gives μ_T(B_r(x)) = M_{B_r(x)}(T) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
key_steps: If μ_T(B_r(x)) = 0 then H^n(M ∩ B_r(x)) = 0, so T vanishes on forms supported in the relatively compact ball B_{s/2}(x), and x ∉ spt T.
If T vanishes near x then M_{B_r(x)}(T) = 0, and mass_eq_weight gives μ_T(B_r(x)) = 0.
